shared_expression_dependencies.rationale: Retain method preference, business transaction and remaining balance. Split payment can describe methods or separate diners' contributions. The question checks an available arrangement and does not establish credit or installment terms.

Retain the recurring business exchange and its price, tax and amount left to pay. Incidental payment also fits the clarified act/amount definition. A statement records the transaction without making recording a lexical requirement.

Retain the existing conditional sequence: verify the declined attempt and status before suggesting another attempt. The sentence does not require retry, and incidental payment keeps the general payment meaning.

Retain both payment approval and arranging payment. These select the act of paying, which is why the canonical definition needs to include the act as well as the paid amount. The authorized reviewer controls the next step.
Retain payment records as records concerning the paying/amount sense. Review of time and rates before finalization does not calculate an entitlement or establish that funds were transferred.

Retain transaction as the business exchange whose accounting entries are compared. The source record is a context, not a defining condition, and debit/credit entries are not the selected payment-card nouns.
Retain incidental transaction in transaction records. The phrase names records of exchanges; transaction is not one of this expression's selected focuses and no route is inferred from its appearance.

Retain proof of purchase as supporting evidence, not necessarily a paper receipt. The required document type depends on the particular claim arrangements.

Retain refund policy as the booking seller's stated payment-return arrangements. The context expressly preserves legal rights and refers the cancellation question instead of announcing a deadline or fee.

Retain warranty as recorded product-assurance information. A service interval and inspection date are separate records; their presence does not establish coverage, inspection validity or a maintenance instruction.
Retain the need to check warranty terms before promising a replacement. A return authorization and an assurance are separate matters; neither guarantees the outcome by itself.
Retain warranty as product-assurance terms requested with the specification. Providing documents for review makes no promise about product performance or remedies.
Retain the specific warranty scope and expiration date check. The context names actual product terms and does not promise a remedy or imply that all legal rights expire with that warranty.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: payment
original_consultation_records.finding: The noun names both paying and an amount paid or expected. Arranging payment and a method of payment are explicit patterns.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: transaction
original_consultation_records.finding: A transaction is a business deal, especially buying or selling. Recording a transaction is an example, not an intrinsic requirement of the meaning.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: sale
original_consultation_records.section: noun sense 1, act or process of selling
original_consultation_records.finding: Selling goods is distinct from the reduced-price-event sense. Examples include a sale that is completed and a sale that falls through; this project retains its narrower completed-selling selection.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: price
original_consultation_records.finding: Price is the money asked or paid for something. It can overlap with a buyer's cost and is not necessarily an amount excluding tax.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: cost
original_consultation_records.finding: Cost covers money needed to buy, make or do something. Both buyer expense and the expense of providing something fit this sense.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: subtotal
original_consultation_records.finding: A subtotal is an intermediate sum that contributes to a final total. The definition does not establish one universal ordering of taxes and discounts.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: balance
original_consultation_records.finding: Balance covers money left after subtraction, money available in an account, and an amount still owed after part has been paid.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: change
original_consultation_records.finding: Money returned after overpayment is the selected sense. The separate coins sense means that coins alone do not uniquely show change returned to a buyer.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: cash
original_consultation_records.finding: The selected physical-money sense refers to notes and coins, distinct from wider informal uses for money or available funds.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: coin
original_consultation_records.finding: A coin is a small metal piece used as money. Being metal alone does not distinguish a coin from a token.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: banknote
original_consultation_records.finding: The dictionary describes paper money and records note in British usage and bill in North American usage. Polymer material is supported separately by the issuing bank.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: debit card
original_consultation_records.finding: A debit card pays using money in a bank account. The source distinguishes it from a credit card; it does not establish overdraft or merchant-acceptance rules.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: credit card
original_consultation_records.finding: A credit card permits a purchase with payment to the issuer later. This is different from direct bank-account spending.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: gift card
original_consultation_records.finding: A gift card carries an amount that can be exchanged for goods or services. Digital codes and non-purchased issuance are supported by the separate provider example.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: voucher
original_consultation_records.finding: A voucher may be a printed document or electronic code giving value, a discount or another stated benefit. The form alone does not distinguish it from a coupon.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: coupon
original_consultation_records.finding: A coupon may be paper or an electronic code that gives a price reduction or other commercial benefit. The financial-security sense is outside this selection.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: loyalty card
original_consultation_records.section: noun definition and British usage label
original_consultation_records.finding: The card identifies a customer in a repeat-purchase scheme. Points and benefits depend on the particular scheme; the British label is recorded without changing regional metadata.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: membership
original_consultation_records.finding: Membership is the state of belonging to a group. It is distinct from the whole set of members and does not inherently mean a fee.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: deposit
original_consultation_records.section: noun sense 1, first part of larger payment
original_consultation_records.finding: The advance-part-payment sense explicitly overlaps with down payment. Bank-account deposits and security deposits are separate senses.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: installment
original_consultation_records.section: noun payment sense and American spelling
original_consultation_records.finding: An instalment is one of a sequence of payments over time. The source gives installment as the American form; both spellings already exist in this entry.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: down payment
original_consultation_records.finding: The noun names the first part of a larger payment. It can be called a deposit; the housing example does not limit the term to mortgages.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: contactless
original_consultation_records.section: adjective technology sense; contactless payment collocation
original_consultation_records.finding: Contactless technology permits a compatible smart card or phone to communicate without a physical connection. Contactless payment is an explicit combination.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: surcharge
original_consultation_records.finding: A surcharge is an additional amount on top of a stated price or charge. The source does not authorize imposing a particular surcharge.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: fee
original_consultation_records.finding: A fee is an amount charged for a service. This supports the ordinary composition service fee without treating it as a voluntary tip.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: tax
original_consultation_records.finding: Tax is money paid under government rules on income, profits, goods or services. No rate or individual liability follows from the lexical definition.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: sales tax
original_consultation_records.finding: Sales tax is a tax on purchases in certain countries. The selected definition appropriately leaves applicability to the jurisdiction.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: tip
original_consultation_records.finding: The service sense is an extra amount given to someone who serves the customer. Advice, an object's pointed end and a waste site are distinct senses.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: cash back
original_consultation_records.finding: The selected sense provides cash with a debit-card purchase and adds that cash to the purchase charge. A promotional refund or reward is a different sense. Cashback and cash-back appear as regional spellings.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: currency
original_consultation_records.finding: Currency is a country's money system; the European currency example also supports money used across a monetary area. The sense does not mean a particular banknote.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: receipt
original_consultation_records.finding: A receipt records payment for goods or services and may be paper or electronic. Receipt of goods and other acknowledgment senses are distinct.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: warranty
original_consultation_records.finding: The product sense gives an assurance about repair or replacement. Individual coverage, exclusions and duration are not fixed by the word itself.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: round
original_consultation_records.finding: Rounding replaces a number with a nearby less precise value. The definition and examples distinguish numerical rounding from making a shape circular.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: refund
original_consultation_records.finding: A refund returns money previously paid, including overpayment or returned goods. Dictionary example policies are not adopted as real customer rights.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: exchange
original_consultation_records.finding: An exchange gives something and receives something in return. The purchased-item context selects replacement goods rather than currency conversion or conversation.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: policy
original_consultation_records.section: noun sense 1, chosen plan of action
original_consultation_records.finding: A business policy is an agreed or chosen course of action. The term is distinct from an insurance contract and does not supersede applicable law.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Selected lexical passage only. Examples are not merchant policy, financial or legal advice, a morphology approval, or permission to reuse source media.

original_consultation_records.title: Bank of England: Why are new banknotes made of polymer?
original_consultation_records.section: When did the Bank of England start printing banknotes?; new note material
original_consultation_records.finding: The issuer explains that its newer notes use thin flexible polymer instead of paper. This supports both materials in banknote.
original_consultation_records.limitation: UK issuing-bank example only. No denomination, circulation date, security-feature reproduction or asset license is imported.

original_consultation_records.title: Shopify: Gift cards considerations and overview
original_consultation_records.finding: A recipient can receive a digital gift card with a unique code redeeming stored value. The provider also permits gift cards issued without a purchase.
original_consultation_records.limitation: One commerce platform, not a guarantee of availability or universal acceptance. The legacy prepaid ID does not require altering the current broader definition.

original_consultation_records.title: Square: Loyalty Program
original_consultation_records.finding: Points are units earned under configured rules and redeemed for defined rewards. Sellers determine the earning and reward arrangements.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Provider-specific examples only; no earning ratio, monetary value, expiry, enrollment requirement or customer data collection is adopted.

original_consultation_records.title: Stripe: Billing addresses
original_consultation_records.section: What is a billing address?; invoicing needs; shipping-address distinction
original_consultation_records.finding: The address is associated with a payment account and billing records. It serves a different purpose from a delivery address and can differ from it.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Payment-provider explanation only. No fraud judgment, mandatory address collection, verification procedure or legal requirement is inferred.

original_consultation_records.title: GOV.UK: How VAT works
original_consultation_records.finding: The source expands VAT as Value Added Tax and identifies it as a tax on products and services supplied by VAT-registered businesses.
original_consultation_records.limitation: UK explanation only. Rates, registration thresholds, calculations and reporting instructions are excluded from the lesson.

original_consultation_records.title: European Commission: How does VAT work?
original_consultation_records.section: Value Added Tax is; How do EU countries apply VAT?
original_consultation_records.finding: VAT is a consumption tax; its practical application varies across EU countries. This supports the broad abbreviation and multi-jurisdiction description.
original_consultation_records.limitation: EU context only. No deduction eligibility, taxpayer status, rate or accounting procedure is approved.

original_consultation_records.title: GOV.UK: Where you see VAT
original_consultation_records.section: In shops; On bills and receipts
original_consultation_records.finding: A separate VAT line may show tax already included in a retail price. A displayed tax line must not automatically be added again.
original_consultation_records.limitation: UK illustration of why price components need checking, not a universal display rule or a tax calculation for the fictional lesson.

original_consultation_records.title: ECB: What is the role of exchange rates?
original_consultation_records.section: What are exchange rates?; reference rates
original_consultation_records.finding: An exchange rate converts between currencies. Published reference rates may differ from actual transaction rates.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Lexical and reference-rate distinction only. No rate, fee, preferred currency or currency-conversion advice is supplied.

original_consultation_records.title: Microsoft: ROUND function
original_consultation_records.finding: Numerical rounding can target a selected number of decimal digits, an integer or another place value. The page also distinguishes rounding to a specified multiple.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Numerical meaning only. Excel procedures and tie-breaking behavior do not establish a merchant or jurisdictional cash-rounding policy.

original_consultation_records.title: Best Buy: Price Match Guarantee FAQs
original_consultation_records.finding: The retailer offers to match qualifying prices subject to product and competitor conditions. The wording illustrates why a price match requires eligibility checks.
original_consultation_records.limitation: One retailer's current policy only. Its exclusions, pre-tax comparison rule, channels, dates and remedies are not transferred to this fictional store.

original_consultation_records.title: Stripe: Coupons and promotion codes
original_consultation_records.section: Coupons versus promotion codes; Set a minimum amount
original_consultation_records.finding: A customer-facing code applies an offer subject to restrictions. A minimum order value can determine whether the code is usable.
original_consultation_records.limitation: The provider's API distinction between coupons and codes is not imposed on ordinary English. No actual discount, minimum amount or automatic entitlement is promised.

original_consultation_records.title: Stripe: Issuing spending controls
original_consultation_records.finding: Amount-based rules specify maximum spending for an authorization or interval. Limits may differ by card, cardholder and category.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Provider implementation only. No amount, universal enforcement guarantee, credit recommendation or permission to change controls is imported.

original_consultation_records.title: Adyen: Create an authorisation
original_consultation_records.finding: The response has an authorization code after successful authorization and an empty field when authorization fails. The field is a transaction reference, not a customer PIN.
original_consultation_records.limitation: One API field supports the selected meaning; the code is not proof of capture, settlement or payout. No card data or live processing is involved.

original_consultation_records.title: Adyen: Payments lifecycle
original_consultation_records.section: Authorization statuses; Capture and settlement statuses
original_consultation_records.finding: Authorization reserves funds and is distinct from capture and settlement. A refused request is not approved; later statuses must be checked separately.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Provider-specific lifecycle explanation, not operational instructions or a universal status model. No code alone establishes final payment.

original_consultation_records.title: Stripe: Card declines
original_consultation_records.finding: A card issuer may decline an attempted transaction for several reasons. The advice code can prohibit another attempt, so a lesson must not presume retry is appropriate.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Provider-specific evidence for neutral wording. No cause of this fictional decline, retry count, collection advice or authorization to retry is claimed.

original_consultation_records.title: Shopify: Multiple and partial payments on Shopify POS
original_consultation_records.section: Accept split payment methods for an entire order
original_consultation_records.finding: One order can be paid using more than one method. The page separately describes partial balances, supporting a distinction from a scheduled installment.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Platform-specific feature with restrictions. No capability, eligibility, procedure or later-payment arrangement is promised for every shop.

original_consultation_records.title: Square: Split a check by item or seat
original_consultation_records.section: About splitting checks; Split a payment
original_consultation_records.finding: A single check can be divided into multiple payment amounts when guests pay separately. This supports contributions as well as different payment types.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Restaurant-provider example only. No checkout method, staff permission or universal merchant support is inferred.

original_consultation_records.title: Shopify: Managing Shopify POS receipts
original_consultation_records.section: Introduction; Send a receipt after a sale
original_consultation_records.finding: Receipts can be printed or sent electronically. A gift receipt is proof of purchase without the amount spent in this implementation.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Provider-specific availability and regional names remain local to the source. The lesson distinguishes format from gift purpose and asks what is available.

original_consultation_records.title: ACCC: Receipts, bills, proof of purchase
original_consultation_records.section: Businesses can ask for proof of purchase
original_consultation_records.finding: Purchase evidence can include a receipt, payment statement or other records linking the buyer and item to the purchase. A receipt is one possible kind of evidence.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Australian guidance only. No evidence sufficiency, mandatory receipt-only policy or universal remedy entitlement is adopted.

original_consultation_records.title: Shopify: Setting up return and cancellation rules
original_consultation_records.finding: The period and the event that starts it are configurable, and rules can vary by market. The term therefore needs an arrangement-specific definition.
original_consultation_records.limitation: Platform-specific examples only. No duration, start date, fee, exclusion or limit on statutory rights is applied to the lesson.

original_consultation_records.title: GOV.UK: Accepting returns and giving refunds
original_consultation_records.finding: A seller cannot remove applicable consumer rights through a no-refund statement. Stated store arrangements and legal rights must be kept distinct.
original_consultation_records.limitation: UK guidance illustrates the limitation only. No rule, deadline, entitlement or legal conclusion is generalized to an unspecified jurisdiction.

original_consultation_records.title: Shopify: Combining discounts
original_consultation_records.finding: Order-level discounts apply to cart subtotals, demonstrating that a subtotal can precede deductions as well as additions.
original_consultation_records.limitation: One platform example only. Discount-combination rules and tax order are not made universal.

original_consultation_records.title: FTC: Warranties
original_consultation_records.finding: A product warranty is a seller or manufacturer assurance with specific coverage and limits. Terms can concern repair, replacement or refund; spoken promises are also discussed.
original_consultation_records.limitation: US guidance only. No mandatory coverage, claim process, free remedy or legal right is asserted for a fictional product.
